scope: Optional original-character formatting-batch rebase delivered through Rust, paired Wasm/SDK, the existing durable revision outbox and borrowed vanilla/React controls. Existing V1 child guards, authenticated finalization, owned Undo and saved meanings remain unchanged. Direct affine text replacement and final V1 qualification are not completed; the full advanced-review goal remains active.
contracts: An ordered batch composed only of SetFormat commands is eligible. Command order and overlapping ranges are preserved. A fragmented child can be rebased again; mixed/non-format commands return Unsupported without discarding a step.

Native source evaluation proves the complete original batch before resolving original scalar identities. Every selected original character must survive in order and in its original protected domain/kind. Reordering, deletion/equal reinsertion, lost boundaries and changed values of the touched format kind refuse the whole batch. Complete typed properties, including Link target fields, are compared; unrelated format kinds survive.

New intervening characters are excluded. The entire lowered batch retains the existing 64-command ceiling, with 65,536 selected scalar occurrences including overlapping steps and 1 MiB of repeated literal bytes counted before cloning. Individual source/range, child/envelope and traversal limits still apply. Exactly 64 lowered steps pass; cumulative or single-range fragmentation above the ceiling refuses without a partial result.

The optional Wasm marker and pure request are separate from complete original revision support. The request contains an exact predecessor, title and creation time, not author authority, a new accepted AST or caller-supplied character/format witnesses. The source observation is checked before parsing. Older complete runtimes retain manual revisions without a JavaScript fallback.

core.rebaseSuggestionFormat returns native Pending/Unsupported/Conflict/Captured. SharedSuggestionRevisions.rebaseFormat checks the exact retained same-creator pending predecessor and queues only Captured bytes. Other outcomes create no revision row. Saved bytes use the unchanged outbox family, source-before-record order, authenticated receipt and committed child-handoff rules. Network or local-save retry never recaptures against a newer source.

The shared vanilla/React action uses the selected proposal's native original intent, not the accepted caret or composer draft. A blank title keeps the prior title. Uncommitted children remain preview-only and cannot independently publish or queue a decision through this outbox. Native preview and authenticated Queue Accept remain separate actions.

Actual authenticated peer edits insert new characters and unrelated marks before capture. Across all six policies, both control variants retain exact offline source/outbox/queue bytes, reopen before supersession, retry original bytes with recapture deliberately disabled, and retain peer text/marks through owned Accept, Undo and Redo. Comment history stays unchanged and the later mixed named-version restore/recovery workflow still passes.

Permanent Readers capture and publish their own formatting revisions without author registration, author resume or document submission. Native authored counters stay zero; Accept remains refused even though proposal supersession is allowed. Host asset bytes, identity, grants and production isolation remain outside content metadata.
verificationNotes: The existing six-policy mixed/Reader/revision matrices retain their assertions and default modes. A separate optional formatting flag adds the new workflows; the normal revision probe does not silently require the new pair.

The installed consumer loads all four production packages, public editor/collaboration exports, its React wrapper and packaged Wasm from clean offline-installed local archives. Strict positive/negative types refuse caller-supplied characters and creator arguments. Test DOM/IDB/locks and loss injection remain fixtures, not physical browser or accessibility evidence.

The new helper does not introduce image assets or fetch their bytes. Existing mixed review workflows exercise image fields/captions and retain asset references; an asset-byte-inclusive advanced-review acceptance case remains separate work.

Strict lint uses no new suppressions beyond the existing marker-method unused_self convention. The pinned engine retains its pre-existing unused-import warning. Canonical native, compatibility, host and Wasm caches remain isolated.
remaining: Direct original-character text insertion/replacement and explicit intervening-peer-text policy without reinterpreting stored V1 intents. Captured formatting children still have ordinary conservative guards for edits after capture.

Asset-byte-inclusive combined advanced-review acceptance with changing anchored targets, offline authors, proposal decisions and named-version restore; preserve host-owned upload/download and retention responsibilities.
Final API/migration, storage lifetime/compaction, package-release and production auth/hosting work, plus deferred broad browser, physical IME, accessibility and performance qualification.
